A1.justification: The authors, research task, corresponding components and extensive matching results identify the same work despite its renaming from CPAny to JustHook. Both PDFs are readable, including their complete appendices, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original Refer-KITTI and Refer-KITTI-V2 experiments, component ablations, runtime measurements and appendix analyses of encoder freezing, scaling and tracker combinations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and additionally reports Refer-Dance evaluation, a cosine-similarity ablation and detector timing.

M1.justification: Grid sampling, motion-feature concatenation, masked parallel decoding and the weighted loss substantially match after renaming CVSA/PSS to VFH/PCD. However, v1 explicitly constructs queries from bounding-box sequences and specifies convolutional FPN connections; v2 describes learnable queries and omits those connections. The PDFs do not establish whether these reflect procedural changes or reduced documentation.

E1.justification: v1's evaluations use KITTI-derived tracking and referring data. v2 adds a separate Refer-Dance evaluation in Appendix E.1 and Table 9, extending evaluated data coverage beyond the retained Refer-KITTI and Refer-KITTI-V2 benchmarks. The task remains referring multi-object tracking.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Within the decoder comparison, v2 adds cosine similarity and removes two sequential-decoding variants. Its encoder-adaptability comparison also drops the iKUN variant with a trainable RoBERTa encoder reported in v1 Table VII.

E3.justification: v2 removes DeiT configurations from the reported experiments and narrows metric reporting by dropping detection/association recall and precision columns. The added Refer-Dance evaluation uses iKUN's supplied detector and tracker outputs. The retained KITTI input resolution, frame sampling, expression sampling, optimizer and 20-epoch training schedule are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct test of replacing PCD with cosine similarity, reduces the sequential-decoder ablation from four variants to two, and removes iKUN's text-unfreezing control. The proposed model's freezing, backbone-scaling, annotation-correction and tracker analyses are retained, as are the qualitative case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present point estimates; references to significant improvements do not introduce statistical testing.

E6.justification: The reported evidence changes substantially through additions and removals, although retained main benchmark scores match exactly. New results include Refer-Dance HOTA of 31.83 for JustHook, 29.06 for iKUN and 9.58 for TransRMOT; cosine-ablation HOTA of 28.29; and detector costs of 12.4 training hours and 2.99 inference minutes. DeiT results, recall/precision entries and several controls disappear. The MLP and parallel-decoder ablation HOTA entries change from 42.82 to 42.81.

T1.justification: The coordinate-grid and entropy-weighted loss mathematics are retained, and neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. v2 adds the standard bilinear-interpolation formula for an operation already specified in v1 and omits the explicit standard cross-entropy formula; these are explanatory changes rather than new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Encoder flexibility, parallel matching, efficiency and the 7.77-point Refer-KITTI-V2 HOTA advantage remain central claims. v2 redefines the contribution around directly exploiting and preserving pretrained contextual processing through a hook-like framework, whereas v1 foregrounds constructing a unified semantic space.

C2.justification: v2 substantially revises the mechanism explanations, attributing advantages to preserving pretrained features and describing cosine matching as prone to collapse outside CLIP's aligned space. Appendix E.2 replaces the earlier freezing explanation with one based on RMOT-specific textual discrimination. New Appendix B discusses data quantity/diversity requirements and claims a tracking-based performance ceiling; v1 has no corresponding limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the detector's approximately 10-epoch training budget, car/pedestrian setup and runtime, and identifies the supplied detection/tracking outputs used for Refer-Dance. Conversely, bounding-box query construction, FPN connections and iKUN's inference stride are no longer explicitly documented. These disclosure changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Both versions still promise future code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds SCLIP and ClearCLIP to support its discussion of CLIP's fine-grained capabilities, plus references on hooking and attention. It removes several references, including DeiT, ViT, LLaMA and PyTorch. The main RMOT literature remains, but the critique of iKUN now stresses disruption of pretrained representations alongside restricted encoder compatibility.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the paper and components, v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, framework explanation and experimental interpretations, while shortening the loss discussion. It reorganizes the supplementary material into Appendices A-F, moves references before the appendices and relocates the main qualitative-results discussion.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column presentation, redraws the framework diagrams, adds bilinear-sampling and motion-aggregation illustrations, and combines decoder illustrations. It removes v1's MOT-versus-RMOT illustration, restructures tables with fewer columns and configurations, and relocates/reformats retained qualitative examples in the appendix.

improvement.justification: Refer-Dance results, the cosine-similarity control and explicit detector overhead strengthen validation and make the efficiency claim more assessable. However, v2 removes the stronger trainable-text iKUN control that achieved 46.23 HOTA in v1 Table VII, reduces reported configurations and metrics, and leaves query/FPN construction less explicit. These gains in coverage and cost transparency coexist with losses in comparative completeness and reproducibility, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
